direction: Optimise centres through the LP value function using dual variables: for fixed centres solve the radii LP with HiGHS, recover the dual weights on the active pair constraints $r_i+r_j\le D_{ij}$, and form the exact centre gradient $\partial(\sum r)/\partial x_i=\sum_j w_{ij}(x_i-x_j)/D_{ij}$ (analogously for $y$), where only contacting pairs contribute. Take projected gradient-ascent steps on centres clipped to $[0.02,0.98]$, with backtracking line search over step sizes such as 0.02 down to $10^{-4}$, accepting a move only if a fresh LP evaluation strictly increases the sum. Alternate these dual-guided centre moves with occasional exact NLP polishing; this directly follows the marginal value of each contact rather than fighting quadratic penalty weights.

idea: Void-relocation topology surgery with simulated-annealing basin hopping on LP-optimal radii plus short penalty L-BFGS repair.
direction: Implement topology surgery by void relocation and basin hopping: after obtaining an incumbent, rasterise a fine grid (e.g. $201\times201$) computing clearance $\min(\min(x,1-x,y,1-y),\min_j(\lVert p-c_j\rVert-r_j))$ to find the largest empty void, then move the smallest or least-contacted circle into that void, or delete and reinsert the $k=1$–$3$ smallest circles at the best void locations found greedily. Follow each surgery with LP radii plus short penalty L-BFGS re-optimisation, accept worsening moves with a simulated-annealing rule $\exp(\Delta/T)$ under a cooling schedule, and periodically restore the elite. This explicitly destroys and rebuilds the contact graph, targeting the filler-circle-plus-residual-void pathology visible in the incumbent.

idea: Centre-only maximisation of the LP-optimal radii sum with diverse stratified initialisations plus greedy single-circle moves and void-relocation ruin-and-recreate to change contact topology.
Active-set LP-dual centre optimisation with fixed-multiplier surrogates plus SLSQP KKT polishing.
direction: Perform exact active-set polishing using the LP dual gradient and equality-constrained nonlinear optimization. Starting from the pictured configuration, its rotations/reflections, and small perturbations, repeatedly solve the fixed-centre radii LP with HiGHS, extract dual multipliers for active pair constraints, and compute the envelope-theorem gradient of the LP-optimal radius sum with respect to the 52 centre coordinates, where each active pair contributes through the derivative of its centre distance. Optimize centres with L-BFGS-B using this gradient, periodically refreshing the active set; then finish with `scipy.optimize.minimize(method="SLSQP")` over all 78 variables, maximizing $\sum r_i$ subject directly to $r_i\le x_i$, $x_i+r_i\le1$, $r_i\le y_i$, $y_i+r_i\le1$, and $r_i+r_j\le\|c_i-c_j\|_2$, supplying analytic constraint Jacobians, tolerances near $10^{-12}$, and adding or removing contact constraints according to gaps and multiplier signs. Apply a final uniform feasibility shrink of about $10^{-9}$ only after optimization, aiming to squeeze the existing basin to a genuinely KKT-balanced, jammed local optimum rather than another penalty approximation.

idea: Structured row-template search with LP-optimal radii scoring via Powell, then jittered centre hill-climbing and annealed joint L-BFGS polish.
direction: Search structured row and deformed-lattice packing families before releasing all coordinates. Enumerate row-count templates compatible with 26 circles, such as $(6,5,6,5,4)$, $(5,6,5,6,4)$, $(6,5,5,5,5)$, $(5,5,6,5,5)$ and staggered hexagonal variants, assigning each row a vertical position, horizontal offset, spacing warp, and either one shared radius class or a smoothly varying radius profile; optimize this roughly 15–25-dimensional parameterization by Nelder–Mead or a small hand-coded CMA-ES using LP-optimal radii for scoring. For the best few templates, break row ties and radius equalities gradually, continue with centre-only LP-gradient optimization, and only then run the full joint SLSQP polish from Direction 1, including templates with approximate vertical, horizontal or 180-degree symmetry as special cases. This directly tests globally different layouts in which every row absorbs part of the extra circle, instead of assuming that an optimal packing must resemble a square grid with interstitial fillers.

idea: Many fast penalty restarts from diverse grids plus iterated ruin-and-recreate using largest-void teleportation, large-small swaps and short rejamming to escape the 5x5 basin before LP-optimal radii.
Delaunay-void-guided topology surgery with simulated annealing over LP-optimal radii.
direction: Implement void-guided discrete topology surgery with simulated annealing on top of LP centre evaluation. From each incumbent, build the Delaunay triangulation of centres augmented by the four square corners, evaluate candidate empty locations at triangle circumcentres and edge midpoints clipped to the square, and score each by its largest feasible empty-circle radius accounting for nearby centres and walls. In each move, delete one to three circles chosen preferentially among the smallest radii or lowest LP-dual pressure, reinsert them sequentially at the largest discovered voids with random jitter, optionally swap the positions of a small filler and a large circle, then run a short dual-gradient or random local centre relaxation and score the result by the exact full LP. Accept worsening surgeries with probability $\exp(\Delta S/T)$ under a decreasing temperature schedule, preserve an elite archive distinguished by sorted neighbour/contact signatures, and devote most of the time budget to surgeries that alter adjacency rather than Gaussian moves that preserve the current $5\times5$-plus-fillers topology.

idea: Lubachevsky-Stillinger growth with pressure-dependent rates, repulsion dynamics, collective kicks/compressions/permutations to generate new contact graphs, followed by exact LP-optimal radii and hill-climbing plus penalized polishing.
direction: Use a physics-inspired Lubachevsky–Stillinger growth simulation as a genuinely different global search engine. Initialize centres randomly, on jittered lattices, and from elite configurations, assign all circles a small common radius, then alternate overlap-resolution steps—pairwise repulsion along centre lines and wall repulsion implemented with analytic displacements or velocity-Verlet dynamics—with slow radius growth whose rate is inversely related to each circle’s current contact pressure or overlap. Periodically introduce collective events such as random centre kicks, radius-role permutations, compression toward a randomly chosen corner, and temporary growth-rate advantages for currently small circles; whenever overlaps fall below a strict threshold, record the configuration, replace radii by the exact LP optimum for those centres, and restart growth from the best few dynamically distinct states. Finish every retained state with LP radii and active-set polishing, using the simulation primarily to generate contact graphs unreachable by smooth penalty descent from the incumbent basin.

idea: Reproduce a feasible incumbent with short annealed L-BFGS plus LP-optimal radii then polish all 78 variables with analytic-Jacobian SLSQP alternated with LP re-optimization and low-contact centre perturbations with strict checkpointing.
direction: Perform incumbent-focused exact-constraint polishing instead of another global penalty search: first reproduce a feasible incumbent near 2.631 using the deterministic seed and pipeline of program 6 for at most 25 seconds, record its centres, radii, active wall contacts, and neighbour pairs whose distance is within \(10^{-4}\) of \(r_i+r_j\), then optimize all 78 variables with `scipy.optimize.minimize(method="SLSQP")` using the exact inequalities \(r_i-x_i\le0\), \(x_i+r_i-1\le0\), \(r_i-y_i\le0\), \(y_i+r_i-1\le0\), and \(r_i+r_j-\lVert c_i-c_j\rVert\le0\) with analytic Jacobians; alternate ten SLSQP rounds with LP re-optimization of radii, after each round promote contacts active within \(10^{-7}\) into the preferred active set and perturb only the centres of circles having fewer than three active contacts along directions that reduce their largest slack. Checkpoint the best strictly feasible solution after uniform shrinking by \(1-10^{-9}\), wrap every optimizer call in `try/except`, enforce a 115-second deadline, and always return the checkpointed incumbent rather than an untested final iterate.

idea: Diverse hexagonal/grid/random starts with annealed joint-penalty L-BFGS plus LP-optimal radii, followed by void-relocation/swap basin-hopping and LP-only single-centre hill-climbing with high-weight jamming polish.
Enumerate staggered row-count templates scored by LP-optimal radii, hill-climb the best centres and rejamm with annealed penalty L-BFGS with safe fallback.
direction: Systematically enumerate staggered row templates that random restarts are unlikely to discover: for every ordered row-count composition of 26 into four or five rows drawn from patterns such as \((6,5,6,5,4)\), \((5,6,5,6,4)\), \((6,5,5,6,4)\), \((5,5,6,5,5)\), \((6,6,5,5,4)\), and their transposes and reversals, parameterize each template by its row heights, horizontal offsets, left and right margins, and one radius scale per row, initially placing circles on a staggered lattice and optimizing this roughly 25-dimensional problem with Nelder-Mead or differential evolution using LP-optimal radii after assigning centres from the template. Take the best three templates, allow an individual radius multiplier and centre displacement for every circle, polish them with the exact LP-plus-centre-descent procedure, and only then release all centres in a short constrained local optimization; this explores regular large-circle backbones with a single defect or filler region while preserving a known feasible fallback and strict time checks.

idea: Centre-only LP for optimal radii combined with penalty L-BFGS restarts, LP hill-climbing, and Delaunay contact-graph least-squares jamming with edge-flip repair.
direction: Explore alternative packings through Delaunay and power-diagram contact graphs: generate candidate neighbour graphs from the incumbent, structured lattices, and perturbed centre sets; for each graph select wall contacts for boundary circles and a spanning set of neighbour tangencies intended to give most circles at least three contacts, formulate the squared tangency residuals \((x_i-x_j)^2+(y_i-y_j)^2-(r_i+r_j)^2=0\) together with selected wall equations \(x_i-r_i=0\), \(1-x_i-r_i=0\), \(y_i-r_i=0\), or \(1-y_i-r_i=0\), and solve them from multiple perturbed starts with `scipy.optimize.least_squares`, rejecting solutions with negative radii or non-graph overlaps. After each graph solve, compute LP-optimal radii, measure slack and contact multiplicity, flip one Delaunay edge or replace one wall contact, and retain the modification only if the LP score improves or if it increases rigidity without losing more than \(0.0002\) in score; run this graph-repair loop from several seeds, checkpoint every feasible result, and terminate safely at 118 seconds with the best checkpoint.

idea: Centre-only LP-optimal basin-hopping with ruin-recreate, swaps, symmetries and void jumps under Metropolis cooling and an elite pool.
direction: Use centre-only basin-hopping where the objective is exactly the LP-optimal sum of radii for 52 centre variables, but add large topology-changing moves unavailable to ordinary Gaussian hill-climbing: starting from the incumbent, repeatedly remove the three smallest circles and greedily reinsert them one at a time at the best point found on a \(41\times41\) grid of candidate centres by recomputing the LP, swap the positions of randomly chosen large and small circles, reflect or rotate the whole centre set by multiples of \(90^\circ\), and occasionally relocate one large circle into the largest empty region identified from a dense grid. Incumbent-focused SLSQP polishing with exact constraints and LP radii re-optimization plus low-contact perturbation.
direction: Perform incumbent-focused exact-constraint polishing instead of another global penalty search: first reproduce a feasible incumbent near 2.631 using the deterministic seed and pipeline of program 6 for at most 25 seconds, record its centres, radii, active wall contacts, and neighbour pairs whose distance is within \(10^{-4}\) of \(r_i+r_j\), then optimize all 78 variables with `scipy.optimize.minimize(method="SLSQP")` using the exact inequalities \(r_i-x_i\le0\), \(x_i+r_i-1\le0\), \(r_i-y_i\le0\), \(y_i+r_i-1\le0\), and \(r_i+r_j-\lVert c_i-c_j\rVert\le0\) with analytic Jacobians; alternate ten SLSQP rounds with LP re-optimization of radii, after each round promote contacts active within \(10^{-7}\) into the preferred active set and perturb only the centres of circles having fewer than three active contacts along directions that reduce their largest slack. Checkpoint the best strictly feasible solution after uniform shrinking by \(1-10^{-9}\), wrap every optimizer call in `try/except`, enforce a 115-second deadline, and always return the checkpointed incumbent rather than an untested final iterate.

idea: Staggered row-count defect templates plus void-insertion homotopy scored by LP-optimal radii then jammed with penalized L-BFGS.
direction: Enumerate structured defect templates that are not $5\times5$ plus noise, including row-count partitions $(6,5,6,5,4)$, $(6,6,5,5,4)$, $(5,6,5,5,5)$, $(4,6,5,6,5)$, and $(6,5,4,6,5)$, together with their transposes and reflections. For each template initialize staggered rows with row-specific $y$-positions, horizontal offsets, and nominal spacings, perturb only those low-dimensional template parameters (row $y$'s, offsets, and a smooth left-to-right radius gradient) under radii-LP scoring for at most 35 seconds total, then release the best two templates to full centre optimization by penalty L-BFGS and LP. In parallel include one homotopy construction: take a good 25-circle $5\times5$ solution, insert the 26th circle with radius near zero at its largest void, and gradually force growth by optimizing all variables in stages with lower bounds on the inserted radius increasing through $0.02,0.04,0.06,0.08$ while other radii are LP-reoptimized, so the lattice is forced to reorganize around a deliberately placed defect rather than merely accepting a tiny filler.

Centre-only LP-dual ascent with envelope gradients averaged over jittered centres inside trust-region L-BFGS-B, seeded by penalty incumbents
direction: Implement centre-only optimization using LP dual sensitivities, reducing the problem from 78 penalty variables to 52 centre variables: for fixed centres solve the radii LP with HiGHS, $r_i+r_j\le d_{ij}$ and $r_i\le b_i=\min(x_i,1-x_i,y_i,1-y_i)$, extract nonnegative pair duals $\lambda_{ij}$ and wall duals $\mu_i$ while explicitly checking HiGHS marginal sign conventions on a tiny finite-difference test, then form the envelope gradient $\nabla_{c_i}S=\sum_j\lambda_{ij}(c_i-c_j)/d_{ij}$ plus the wall contribution from $\mu_i$ applied only to the currently nearest wall direction. Optimize centres with L-BFGS-B inside bounds $[0.02,0.98]^2$, use a trust-region cap of about $0.02$ per accepted centre move, and stabilize degenerate duals by averaging gradients over the exact centre and four deterministically jittered centres with jitter $10^{-5}$. Verify every trial centre by a fresh LP, keep the best strictly feasible radii after a $(1-10^{-7})$ shrink, stop by 115 seconds, and fall back to the best penalty incumbent on any dual-sign, LP, or exception failure; this gives exact objective gradients for closing active gaps rather than distorted penalty gradients.
